metrics.method: Manual read of all 401 non-service messages in data/chats/barbara-x-altr.jsonl (2026-07-20 -> 2026-09-17): 218 from the client (Barb Brazil, per config/clients.yaml) and 183 from our side (Stephski 33, Mayson 32, Olivia 31, Michelle 27, Derrek 25, Mica 20, Vivek 15 — all direct ALTR staff per config/team.yaml; no vendor chat team operates in this chat). 'Client question' = a client message containing an explicit ask, whether or not punctuated with '?'; a multi-message ask counts once (the Sep 14 retention message counts as two: the numbers question and the plan request). A naive '?' count over the raw file gives 36; the manual count is higher because many asks are unpunctuated. 'Unanswered >24h' = never answered, answered only after 24h, or answered with no substance (a tag, an emoji, 'Working on it!!'). Note the split: only 1 of 36 punctuated questions waited >24h for ANY reply, and the median gap from a client question to the next message from our side is 43 minutes — the 22 figure is about answers, not speed. 'Promise' = an explicit first-person commitment by our side to do or send something; 'kept' = evidenced in chat; 'lapsed' = never delivered and never mentioned again; 3 further commitments made Sep 17 are still in-window and counted as neither. max_team_silence_days computed from consecutive our-side timestamps: 3.82d (Sep 10 18:04 -> Sep 14 13:43), then 3.77d (Sep 4 -> Sep 8) and 3.19d (Aug 27 -> Aug 30).

top_fix: Give this account one named owner who closes loops in writing, and make a weekly written status with at least one real number the non-negotiable deliverable. Everything that went wrong here is the same failure: we answer in 43 minutes and we close in never — 17 lapsed promises, 22 unanswered asks, a self-written rescue plan sitting 25 days without a yes or no, and a retention warning that got a call offer and no call. A single owner posting 'here is what we posted, here is what it did, here is every open item with a date' every Friday would have surfaced the traffic collapse in week two instead of letting her discover it in her own dashboard in week eight, and would have made it impossible for a Meta-support rep to re-promise the same account recovery twice in six days while the client's last working Instagram died.
